posts.title: Closing the Thirty-Day Cash Gap: How European Small Suppliers Protect Working Capital
posts.excerpt: When corporate customers take thirty to sixty days to pay for delivered goods, invoice factoring offers independent suppliers a calm, reliable way to fund materials and payroll without debt.
posts.content:
Every Monday morning across Europe, thousands of independent workshop owners and producers experience the exact same operational friction. A major commercial order has been manufactured, carefully packaged, and signed for at the client's receiving dock. The sale is complete and the client is satisfied. Yet the invoice terms specify payment in thirty, forty-five, or sixty days, while the supplier must pay staff on Friday and purchase raw materials today for the next production run. This gap between delivery and cash receipt is the quiet stress point of small European business.

Azuke Finance B.V. was founded in 2019 in Rotterdam to address this specific structural hurdle. Operating from Haringvliet 92 in Rotterdam, co-founders Ines Vercauteren and Tomás Aldana set out to replace the punitive terms of legacy factoring with a calm, transparent alternative. Traditional factoring institutions historically demanded whole-ledger turnover commitments, personal director debentures, and opaque monthly retainers that tied up owners in administrative red tape. In contrast, Azuke Finance operates on a selective, per-invoice model with zero application fees, zero monthly maintenance charges, and no minimum invoice volume.

The mechanics are deliberately straightforward. When an EU-registered business completes a commercial delivery, they upload one invoice between €1,000 and €150,000 alongside its signed delivery note or completion document. Underwriting lead Priya Raman and her team review the submission within one working day, evaluating the completed fulfillment and the credit standing of the corporate debtor rather than demanding years of balance sheet records. Upon verification, Azuke Finance advances 90% of the invoice value directly to the supplier's business IBAN on the next working day. An optional same-day payout is available for €25 when approval occurs before 13:00 CET.

The real value of this immediate liquidity is evident in everyday operations across diverse sectors. In Antwerp, Maren Holt of Holt Paper Goods completed an €8,600 packaging order for a retail chain on 45-day terms. Rather than halting her presses, Maren accessed an advance the next working day, purchasing fresh board reels the same week to fulfill subsequent client orders. In Lyon, Felipe Duarte of Duarte Bakehouse supplied a €3,200 wholesale pastry order to a hotel group on 30-day terms, using his 90% advance to secure bulk flour and ingredients for the peak holiday season. In Cologne, Sun-hee Park of Park Print Studio billed an event agency €21,000 on 60-day terms, using the facility to pay two freelance textile specialists promptly upon project sign-off.

Transparency extends directly to the cost structure. The funding fee is fixed at 1.4% of the invoice value for the first 30 days, with 0.7% added for each subsequent 15 days if the customer settles late, up to an absolute cap of 4.2%. When the corporate buyer pays the invoice, Azuke Finance remits the remaining 10% reserve minus the single agreed fee. Supplier relations lead Jonas Weber and customer support lead Amara Okoye support suppliers throughout this process from Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 17:30 CET.

By aligning cash flow with the physical reality of completed work, independent European producers no longer have to function as uncompensated banks for their corporate buyers. Clear, predictable invoice funding provides the breathing room businesses need to protect their margins, honor commitments to staff, and invest in steady, sustainable growth.
